# A cache has an SLO or it has a feeling

## WHY

"I added a cache" is not an outcome. The outcomes are two numbers: the **hit ratio** (the share of
lookups the cache answered) and the **origin calls** (how often the store was asked anyway). The
first is the cache's own health; the second is what the store pays for it — and a ratio without the
second is how a cache that is "99% effective" sits in front of a store that is dying.

An SLO makes the ratio operationally useful: a threshold, a window, and a verdict. Two boundary
decisions matter more than the arithmetic:

- **an empty window is healthy.** A service with no traffic has no hit ratio and is not failing; a
  `0.0` here would page somebody at 3 a.m. for a quiet night;
- **the boundary belongs to healthy.** A ratio exactly at the SLO is not an incident. `>` instead of
  `>=` turns every on-target window into an alert, and an alert that fires every time is one nobody
  reads.

## TASK

The scaffold added `src/effectiveness.rs` and its `pub mod effectiveness;` line. `report` (the
counting) and `lookups`/`origin_calls` are given.

- **[`Report::ratio`]** — hits divided by lookups; `1.0` when nothing was asked.
- **[`verdict`]** — [`Verdict::Healthy`] at or above the SLO, [`Verdict::BelowSlo`] below it.

## DONE WHEN

- `kiln run cache/6.7-cache-effectiveness` — the spec passes
- `kiln check cache/6.7-cache-effectiveness` — every must gate is green
- nine hits out of ten against a `0.9` SLO is healthy, and eight out of ten is not

## TRAP

1. **Dividing by zero.** `hits as f64 / lookups as f64` on an empty window is `NaN`, and `NaN >= 0.9`
   is `false` — every quiet window becomes an incident. The spec's *"an empty window is healthy"* is
   this defect.
2. **`>` instead of `>=`.** The boundary second of arithmetic: a ratio of exactly `0.9` against a
   `0.9` SLO is healthy.
3. **Counting every shared hit as a miss.** In a two-layer cache the shared hit did not reach the
   origin; a ratio that counts it as a miss understates the cache and misleads the capacity plan.
4. **Reporting a ratio without the origin count.** `1.0` on two lookups is true and meaningless; the
   number that matters is how many calls the store actually saw.

## FURTHER

- [Redis: `INFO stats`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/info/) — the counters a real cache
  exports, and the ratio computed from them
- [Caching best practices (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/caching/best-practices/) — hit ratio as a
  capacity input rather than a vanity metric
